name: Sri Gnana Saraswathi Devasthanam
address: Executive Officer, Sri Gnana Saraswathi Devasthanam, Basara, Nirmal District, Telangana - 504101
description:
Abode of Goddess Sri Gnana Saraswathi Devi – at Basara village of Nirmal District in Telangana State is one of the ancient and famous Shaivite & Saraswathi temples. Sri Gnana Saraswathi temple at Basara on the banks of river Godavari is the only temple in South India dedicated to the Goddess of learning.
The Institution is under the Endowments Department, Government of Telangana. The shrine deserves a special mention in terms of its architectural grandeur, serene spiritual atmosphere, and ancient historical sanctity.
history: Established by Maharshi Veda Vyasa after the Mahabharata war. The place was originally called 'Vyasapuri' and gradually evolved into 'Basara'.
mythology: The legend has it that after the Mahabharata war, Sage Veda Vyasa embarked on a pilgrimage in search of peace. He reached the serene Kumaranchala hills on the banks of river Godavari, meditated and propitiated the Goddess who eventually appeared before him and granted her presence in the form of the divine trinity (Goddess Saraswathi, Goddess Lakshmi, and Goddess Kali).
redevelopment_notice: CRITICAL VISITOR NOTICE (July 2026 – 2028): The main stone sanctum sanctorum (Garbhagudi) of the Basara Temple was officially closed to the public on July 5, 2026, for a massive two-year reconstruction project. The sacred presiding deity has been shifted to a temporary wooden shrine known as the Balalayam. All daily darshans, poojas, and Akshara Abhyasam (child learning initiation ceremonies) are operating normally from this temporary structure, but visitors should expect a smaller prayer area.Crucial Temple Redevelopment Notice: The primary temple structure is currently undergoing a massive ₹225 crore transformation. Because of this, all main rituals, darshans, and Aksharabhyasam sevas have been systematically moved to a temporary, downsized structure called the Bala Alayam.
